source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: The client stops inhaling when the examiner presses below the right costal margin. This is:
questions.rationale: Murphy's sign indicates cholecystitis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cholecystitis (PDF p. 353)
questions.quote: Murphy's sign- Pain on taking a deep breath

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Gallstone pain typically occurs in the RUQ and may radiate to the:
questions.rationale: Biliary colic radiates to the back near the right scapular tip.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cholelithiasis (PDF p. 353)
questions.quote: possibly radiating to the back or near the right scapular tip

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is the diagnostic procedure of choice for gallstones?
questions.rationale: Ultrasound is the procedure of choice.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Gallbladder Diagnostics (PDF p. 353)
questions.quote: Ultrasonography- diagnostic procedure

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which diet should a client with cholelithiasis follow?
questions.rationale: Low-fat diet reduces gallbladder stimulation and colic.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Gallbladder Management (PDF p. 353)
questions.quote: Low-fat liquids

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Ursodeoxycholic acid is used to:
questions.rationale: UDCA dissolves small radiolucent gallstones.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Gallbladder Pharmacology (PDF p. 353)
questions.quote: dissolve small radiolucent gall stone

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Using shock waves to fragment gallstones without incision is:
questions.rationale: ESWL is noninvasive fragmentation of stones.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Gallbladder Management (PDF p. 353)
questions.quote: Non-invasive procedure; uses repeated shock waves

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: The biliary drainage tube is clamped 1 hour before and after meals in order to:
questions.rationale: Clamping lets bile flow into the duodenum to aid fat digestion.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Biliary Drainage (PDF p. 354)
questions.quote: to allow bile to the duodenum to aid in digestion

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Acute pancreatitis is self-digestion of the pancreas mainly by:
questions.rationale: Activated trypsin and other proteolytic enzymes digest the pancreas.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Acute Pancreatitis (PDF p. 354)
questions.quote: principally trypsin

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Bluish discoloration around the umbilicus in acute pancreatitis is:
questions.rationale: Cullen's: periumbilical; Grey Turner's: flank, indicating retroperitoneal bleeding.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Acute Pancreatitis (PDF p. 354)
questions.quote: Cullen's sign- bluish discoloration around the umbilicus

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which lab results support acute pancreatitis?
questions.rationale: Elevated amylase, lipase, and WBC; hypocalcemia may occur.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Acute Pancreatitis (PDF p. 354)
questions.quote: Elevated amylase

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Why is a client with acute pancreatitis kept NPO?
questions.rationale: NPO inhibits pancreatic stimulation and enzyme secretion.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Acute Pancreatitis (PDF p. 354)
questions.quote: The client should avoid oral intake to inhibit pancreatic stimulation

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Frothy, foul-smelling, fatty stools in chronic pancreatitis are called:
questions.rationale: Impaired fat digestion causes steatorrhea; give pancreatic enzymes with meals.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Chronic Pancreatitis (PDF p. 354)
questions.quote: Stools become frequent, frothy, and foul-smelling

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Chronic pancreatitis may lead to which endocrine complication?
questions.rationale: Islet cell damage causes diabetes; glucose tolerance becomes abnormal.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Chronic Pancreatitis (PDF p. 355)
questions.quote: Manage any endocrine insufficiency such as Diabetes Mellitus

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with a perforated ulcer has a rigid, board-like abdomen and rebound tenderness. This suggests:
questions.rationale: Peritonitis: rigidity, rebound tenderness, ileus, fever, tachycardia.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Peritonitis (PDF p. 355)
questions.quote: Muscles become rigid and tender

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which position decreases pain in a client with peritonitis?
questions.rationale: Knees flexed decreases tension on abdominal organs.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Peritonitis Nursing (PDF p. 356)
questions.quote: Patient is placed on the side with knees flexed

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which hormone is released by the posterior pituitary?
questions.rationale: Posterior pituitary releases ADH and oxytocin.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Posterior Pituitary (PDF p. 357)
questions.quote: Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH)/ Vasopressin

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Aldosterone acts on the kidney to:
questions.rationale: Mineralocorticoids increase sodium absorption and potassium loss.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Adrenal Cortex (PDF p. 358)
questions.quote: Increase sodium absorption, potassium loss by kidney.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Calcitonin from the thyroid gland:
questions.rationale: Calcitonin lowers calcium; parathormone raises it.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Thyroid Gland (PDF p. 358)
questions.quote: Lower blood calcium and phosphate levels.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Why is serum calcium monitored after thyroidectomy?
questions.rationale: Parathyroid glands may be removed or injured, causing hypocalcemia.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Parathyroid Glands (PDF p. 358)
questions.quote: they are often difficult to locate and can be removed accidentally

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Glucagon from pancreatic alpha cells:
questions.rationale: Glucagon stimulates glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pancreatic Islet Cells (PDF p. 358)
questions.quote: Increases blood glucose concentration

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which hormone is produced by the kidney to stimulate RBC production?
questions.rationale: Erythropoietin increases RBC production; renin activates RAAS.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Kidney Hormones (PDF p. 359)
questions.quote: Erythropoietin

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Gigantism results from excess growth hormone when:
questions.rationale: GH excess before epiphyseal closure causes gigantism; after closure, acromegaly.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Gigantism (PDF p. 359)
questions.quote: Epiphyseal plate still open.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with a GH-secreting pituitary tumor reports headache and diplopia. These are due to:
questions.rationale: Pituitary tumors press on the optic chiasm and raise ICP.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Gigantism (PDF p. 359)
questions.quote: Tumor of somatotrophs (signs of increased ICP)
